thread:
priya: FYI P1 from AcmeLabs on dedicated pool ded-42 in ap-northeast-1a — since ~03:10 UTC their token throughput dropped ~60%. Customers see lots of 429s + long tail latency. Raising to eng-runtime for triage.

mike: Can you paste sample request_ids and last 10m of batcher metrics? Any recent rollout on that pool?

priya: Request ids: req-9f2, req-9f3, req-9f7. No rollout that window. Posting minimal repro curl and a snippet of their app load pattern: many parallel short prompts.

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwkv-7b","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64,"client_request_id":"req-9f2"}'
```

kai: ops-bot flagged an autoscale error at 03:11: `autoscaler: node_init_timeout` and a flurry of docker pull errors in the infra logs. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/cluster/ded-42 (internal).

ops-bot: [ALERT] autoscaler failed to provision 2 nodes for ded-42 due to node init timeout (03:11:24) - retrying.

mike: Looking at batcher telemetry: continuous_batcher average batch_tokens dropped to ~40 tokens, while `max_batch_tokens` on the pool is 128. That leads to many tiny microbatches -> throughput collapse. Also `prefill_merge` was OFF for this pool (was toggled last month). Hypothesis: client sending many short 32-token requests + prefill merge disabled -> inefficient packing.

priya: Customer confirms they set client-side max_response_tokens=32 to save cost and are fanout-ing requests across 150 concurrent connections. They didn't intend to hammer but pattern results in tiny batches. Repro steps I ran locally: run a loadgen with 200 rps of 32-token requests -> observe throughput drop and 429s from serving layer.

jordan: Mitigations to apply now: 1) enable ingress coalescing flag for that ingress (ephemeral) 2) raise `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 on ded-42 canary 3) bump burst_capacity by +2 nodes temporarily. I'll open a canary change and watch.

anna: On SRE side, checking for noisy-tenant signs — looks like one tenant is occupying ~70% of batch slots (tenant id t-77). We should enforce fair-queueing per-tenant to stop head-of-line blocking while we tune scheduler.

mike: We have knobs: `tenant_batch_share` and `min_batch_fill`. Propose tenant_batch_share=0.2 for t-77 and min_batch_fill=0.5 to avoid accepting tiny microbatches for that tenant. Also re-enable `prefill_merge` to allow prefix coalescing and KV warmup to reduce coldstart overhead.

priya: Quick verification from the customer: they can hold off some parallelism if we can show ETA for fix. I've scheduled a 15:00 UTC call.

billing-bot: No billing anomalies detected for ded-42 in the timeframe — charges are normal.

mike: Action items: (1) I will push scheduler tweaks to canary (max_batch_tokens=1024, prefill_merge=ON) and monitor. (2) Anna to apply tenant fair-queue caps. (3) Kai to follow up on the node_init_timeout root cause (docker registry throttling?) and confirm node joins. (4) Jordan to enable ingress coalescing flag.

kai: Initial follow: node_init_timeout was due to transient image pull failures from our internal mirror; registry returned 503s during scale event. That's separate but worsened impact because autoscale couldn't add capacity. Filing infra ticket.

priya: Customer updated: they observed improved qps in canary after scheduler tweak but still seeing occasional spikes. We'll keep monitoring and share postmortem.

jordan: Rolling back not required so far, canary looks stable after 30m. I'll proceed to gradual rollout if no regressions.

mike: Suggest longer-term: add automatic coalescing at the gateway, and consider adaptive `max_batch_tokens` per workload (based on recent token-length distribution).

priya: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and close the P1 once the rollout is complete and autoscale root cause addressed.

anna: +1. Adding notes to incident ticket and tagging support/sre on followups.

ops-bot: [INCIDENT] P1: ded-42 throughput degradation - mitigated by scheduler changes and tenant caps. Incident owner: priya.

priya: Closing notes: repro steps and mitigations saved to the incident doc: https://confluence.internal.incidents/ded-42-throughput-drop (internal).
